alt_text.en: Connect the idea. Read f as the slope of F, not as the height of F. Graph: f first: y=2*x on [0, 1]; f middle: y=3-x on [1, 3]; f last: y=6-2*x on [3, 4]. x-range [0, 4], y-range [-2.6, 2.6].

notes.en: The final negative triangle subtracts one.

notes.en: F has an extremum where f changes sign, not necessarily where f has its own extremum.

notes.en: Using the same graph, find F′(2) and F″(2).

alt_text.en: Your turn. Using the same graph, find F′(2) and F″(2).
alt_text.ko: 직접 풀어보세요. 같은 그래프로 F′(2)와 F″(2)를 구하세요.

prompt.en: Using the same graph, find F′(2) and F″(2).

answer.en: F′(2)=1 and F″(2)=−1. On the middle segment f=3−x, so its height is 1 and slope is −1.
answer.ko: F′(2)=1, F″(2)=−1입니다. 가운데 구간은 f=3−x이므로 높이는 1, 기울기는 −1입니다.

caption.en:
AP Calculus AB • L44
Accumulation function graphs

An accumulation graph rises where its integrand is positive, even if the integrand is falling.
Read f as the slope of F, not as the height of F.

1. The positive triangle adds 3 to the initial value 1.
2. The final negative triangle subtracts one.
3. f changes from positive to negative, so F turns from increasing to decreasing.

Remember: F has an extremum where f changes sign, not necessarily where f has its own extremum.

CHECK ANSWER — try card 8 first
F′(2)=1 and F″(2)=−1. On the middle segment f=3−x, so its height is 1 and slope is −1.
